components.css: .ds-stage{position:relative;width:280px;height:280px;border-radius:20px;background:var(--plate,#f3f6fb);overflow:hidden;font-family:var(--font-sans,'Hanken Grotesk',system-ui,sans-serif)}.ds-lens{position:absolute;left:56px;top:56px;width:168px;height:168px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:50%;border:3px solid var(--ember,#f03c36);background:var(--plate,#f3f6fb);box-shadow:0 22px 44px -12px rgba(0,0,0,.45),inset 0 3px 8px rgba(255,255,255,.55),inset 0 -6px 14px rgba(0,0,0,.18);transition:transform 300ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)}.ds-stage:hover .ds-lens{transform:translate(20px,-12px)}.ds-magnify{position:absolute;top:12px;right:12px;padding:8px 12px;border:0;border-radius:9999px;background:var(--glass-thin-bg,rgba(255,255,255,.46));-webkit-backdrop-filter:blur(18px) saturate(175%);backdrop-filter:blur(18px) saturate(175%);box-shadow:var(--glass-inner,inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.75));color:var(--ink,#0b1a33);font:600 12px/1 var(--font-sans,'Hanken Grotesk',system-ui,sans-serif);cursor:pointer}.ds-magnify:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--brand,#1653a6);outline-offset:3px}

narrative.overview:
Zetra is a maker's bench seen through glass. Every surface is a liquid-glass pane floating over a slow, luminous field of drifting blue, cyan and faint ember light with a fine grain. Panes come in three tiers of thickness, each with a 1px specular edge, an inner highlight and a soft blue-tinted offset shadow. The parts themselves never sit on glass directly: every product photo rests on a light, opaque photo plate, so components read the same in both themes, the way they would on a white bench mat.

The system is dense where people work and generous where they decide. The storefront uses large panes, a big headline and a tilted stack of thick-glass part tags; account, checkout and the admin shell use the same materials more calmly, leaning on thick glass for forms, tables and summaries. One signature interaction carries the world: the Loupe, a red-ringed glass magnifier that reads chip markings off a product photo.

Colour is disciplined. Brand blue does the work (primary actions, active states, focus, the cart count). Logo red appears as a single ring on the Loupe. Status colours (green, amber, deep red) speak only for stock and errors. Type is one family, Hanken Grotesk, from 84px headlines to 11px tab labels; JetBrains Mono appears only where a value is data.
keyCharacteristics: Three glass tiers (thin chrome, regular cards, thick forms/tables/summaries) with honest fallbacks for no backdrop-filter, reduced transparency, forced colours and reduced motion.
A slow ambient field (three drifting radial lights plus grain) behind everything, fixed and non-interactive.
A light photo plate under every product photo, in both themes.
Pill and generously rounded silhouettes; glass droplets slide between active options.
Light and dark themes defined token-for-token; dark is a deep navy field, not grey.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Ember (#f03c36) is the Loupe ring. Destructive actions and out-of-stock use Fault Red (danger), low stock uses Solder Amber; no other surface takes the logo red.

rules.name: The Blue Does The Work Rule
rules.body: Every primary action, active state, focus indicator and the cart count are brand blue. There is no second accent.

rules.name: The Plate Rule
rules.body: Every product photo, thumbnail and the Loupe lens sit on the Photo Plate, in both themes. The dark-theme plate (#dde3ec) stays light so cut-out photos multiply cleanly.

rules.name: The Data Only Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono appears only on values a person might copy, compare or count: spec values, order and payment IDs, quantities. Headings, labels, prices and UI never use it.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase tracked labels anywhere, including the footer.

rules.name: The Three Tiers Rule
rules.body: Thin (46% fill, 18px blur) for chrome: navbar, icon buttons, segmented controls, glass buttons, the Magnify chip. Regular (60%, 24px) for cards, the hero stage and the mobile tab bar. Thick (82%, 28px) for forms, tables, summaries, dialogs, sheets, toasts and the admin sidebar.

rules.name: The Honest Fallback Rule
rules.body: Without backdrop-filter, or under prefers-reduced-transparency, glass becomes opaque glass-solid with no blur. Under forced-colors the rim is replaced by a 1px CanvasText border. Under reduced motion panes do not move, the hero does not rise in, the field does not drift and droplets jump instead of slide.

dos: Do pick a glass tier by role: thin for chrome, regular for cards and stages, thick for anything a person reads or fills in at length.
Do put every product photo on the Photo Plate (plate token) in both themes, with the photo multiplied onto it.
Do use brand blue for primary actions, focus, active states and the cart count.
Do keep the ember ring on the Loupe, and use danger for destructive actions and out-of-stock, warn for low stock.
Do set spec values, order IDs, payment IDs and quantities in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do honour the four fallbacks (no backdrop-filter, reduced transparency, forced colours, reduced motion) on any new glass surface by using the shared glass material.
Do move selection with a sliding glass droplet on the spring curve, and lift interactive panes 3px on the liquid curve.
donts: Don't use logo red (ember) for buttons, badges, prices, links, the footer or decoration.
Don't put product photos directly on glass or on the dark field.
Don't set headings, labels, prices or navigation in mono.
Don't use uppercase, letter-spaced labels or eyebrows above headings.
Don't introduce a second accent colour; status hues are for status only.
Don't hand-roll a translucent surface with its own blur; it will skip the fallbacks.
